correctness.rationale: The proof first proves iff LD-set/complement-transversal using bipartite false twins and domination, then proves k<=4 and excludes k=4 for N>=5 by a three-singleton contradiction. For k=3, each coalition edge corresponds exactly to the third class being transversal, so admissibility is exactly two transversal classes plus no LD class. It counts three unique disjoint families when N>=7 and all finite N=4,5,6 profiles analytically; k=2 follows by excluding proper LD blocks, with no double counting for N>=5. Code independently enumerated all unordered partitions, using direct open-neighborhood LD tests, for all 2<=m<=n with m+n<=10, including triangle graph classification, and directly checked the constructed families in five larger cases. The finite replay corroborates the algebraic proof and does not replace it.

value.rationale: The theorem fully enumerates all allowable unordered class partitions for a natural infinite two-parameter graph family, classifies every maximum partition as one of three concrete transversal patterns, and determines exceptional triangular coalition graphs. This is stronger than the scalar coalition maximum or textbook LD-set minimum: for N>=7 it simultaneously quantifies an exponential two-block count and a polynomial-size optimal three-block family. The exact structure is independently motivated by enumeration of the newly introduced coalition invariant and is mathematically useful without a downstream general theorem.
